qs_015:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose a cloud document storage provider ({{vendor}}) for our company's shared document system. This is a judgment call I need to make personally, so your job is to research and prepare a clear comparison, not to pick or commit to a vendor.

If you don't already know them, ask me for: our team size, rough budget per user/month, whether we need enterprise features (SSO, admin console), and any must-have integrations (e.g. specific office suite, e-signature tools).

Then research 3-4 leading {{vendor}} candidates in the cloud-storage space and build a comparison covering:
1. Desktop sync clients — confirm official macOS/Windows apps exist with selective sync and on-demand/online-only file support.
2. Free tier — does a real free plan exist, and what is its published storage quota; does it use the same clients/API as paid plans.
3. Permissions model — folder- and file-level roles (viewer/commenter/editor/owner), and how inheritance works, per public documentation.
4. Pricing — published per-plan storage quotas and per-user costs, and what happens when a plan's storage cap is hit (e.g. throttling, forced upgrade, read-only).

Present findings in a table (one row per candidate, one column per capability above), with source links or citations for each claim. Add a short recommendation paragraph noting tradeoffs (e.g. cheapest vs. most granular permissions vs. best free tier), but do not declare a final winner.

Done looks like: a complete comparison table plus recommendation summary ready for me to review, with no vendor account created or purchase made.

Report back with the comparison table, your recommendation notes, and then stop for human sign-off so I can make the final selection.

qs_015:n2.prompt:
You are helping me complete the next step in setting up our company's shared document storage system: creating the account and building the initial folder structure. 

First, ask me for any of the following if you don't already have them: (1) which document storage provider I want to use (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365/SharePoint, Box, Dropbox Business), (2) my company name and preferred workspace/domain name, (3) the primary admin email address to use for signup, and (4) the top-level departments or categories I want reflected in the folder structure (e.g., Finance, HR, Legal, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations) plus any known subfolders.

Once I provide these, please:
1. Go to the provider's official signup/console page and create the company account using my configured credentials, entering the company name, domain, and admin email I gave you.
2. Complete the workspace setup steps in the console (organization name, basic settings) as prompted by the provider.
3. Once the account is active, use the provider's web console to create the top-level folders I specified, and add sensible subfolders under each (e.g., under Finance: Invoices, Budgets, Tax; under HR: Policies, Onboarding, Payroll) unless I've told you otherwise.
4. Set basic sharing/access defaults for each top-level folder if the console makes this straightforward (e.g., restrict to internal members by default).

When done, report back with: the provider used, the workspace/domain name, confirmation the account is active, the full folder tree you created, and any default sharing settings applied. Flag anything you couldn't complete (e.g., domain verification pending, payment method required) so I know what's outstanding.

qs_015:n3.prompt:
You are helping me complete the "Share the workspace with the team" step of setting up our company's shared document system. The workspace/provider has already been chosen and configured in an earlier step. If you don't already know it from context, ask me: (1) which document storage provider we're using (e.g., Google Workspace/Google Drive, Microsoft 365/SharePoint, Dropbox Business, Box), (2) the name/location of the shared drive or workspace to grant access to, (3) the full list of team members (names and email addresses) who need access, and (4) the permission level each person should have (e.g., viewer, commenter, editor, or admin).

Once you have this information, use your configured credentials to access the provider's admin console or sharing settings and grant each listed team member access to the shared drive at the specified permission level. Where the provider supports it, also confirm or set sensible default sharing settings for the workspace (e.g., restricting external sharing unless specifically needed). Verify each person's access was successfully granted — either by checking the members/permissions list in the admin console or by confirming via any provider-generated invitation status.

Done looks like: every team member on my list has been added to the shared workspace with the correct permission level, and you've confirmed each grant succeeded (no pending or failed invitations).

Report back with: the provider used, a table or list of each team member with their assigned permission level and access status (confirmed/pending), and any people who couldn't be added along with the reason why.

qs_015:n4.prompt:
You are helping me import our existing company documents into the shared document storage system we've already set up. Please start by asking me for anything you need that isn't already clear: (1) which storage provider we're using (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, Microsoft OneDrive/SharePoint, Box, or Notion), (2) where our existing documents currently live (a local folder, an old shared drive, email attachments, another cloud service, etc.), and (3) the folder/category structure I want in the new workspace (e.g., by department, by document type, by date).

Once you have this, using my configured credentials for the storage provider: (a) create the top-level folder structure I described inside the workspace, (b) transfer the documents from their current location into the correct folders, preserving original filenames and, where the tool supports it, original creation/modified dates, (c) skip or clearly flag duplicate files rather than overwriting anything silently, and (d) verify the transfer by checking that file counts and folder contents match the source location.

If the source is a service that requires a migration or export/import feature, use that feature and describe each action in plain terms rather than referencing any specific API call. If any documents fail to transfer (permission issues, unsupported file types, size limits), keep a list of these failures with reasons.

When finished, report back: the final folder structure created, total number of files successfully imported, any files that failed with reasons, and any duplicates you flagged for my review. Do not delete the original source files — leave them in place until I confirm the migration is complete.
